recent_posts.title: The Economist's Mind as Beach Reading
recent_posts.summary: Three small, accessible books provide a lively introduction to economics for readers without a background in the subject. These books are 'The Armchair Economist' by Steven Landsburg, 'Hidden Order' by David Friedman, and 'Economics in One Lesson' by Henry Hazlitt. Each book offers different perspectives and methods but shares the common goal of making economics understandable and engaging. Additional readings and other notable economics books are suggested for those interested in exploring the field further.

recent_posts.title: Ask First, Code Later: The single, most important question
recent_posts.summary: Developers should question project requirements rather than blindly implementing them. By asking 'why' and engaging in early discussions, they can uncover the true reasons behind requests, thereby leading to better solutions. Collaborative conversations during the requirement phase help address corner cases and find optimal solutions. It's a reminder that questioning and peer-reviewing requirements can lead to more efficient and effective outcomes.

recent_posts.title: Good managers are hard to find and once you have them, they should be appreciated
recent_posts.summary: Good managers are crucial for a thriving organizational culture and employee retention. They have a significant impact on assigning responsibilities, coaching, and mentoring. The post highlights the qualities of good managers, such as leadership, team playing, providing constructive feedback, and fostering growth. Managers face many challenges, including multitasking, stakeholder communication, and ensuring team success. Appreciation for good managers is essential for maintaining a high-performing organization.

recent_posts.title: A Tribute to My Readers and a Bit More
recent_posts.summary: The author reflects on their willingness to protect others despite a general disdain for most people. They critique the Midwestern Doctor's alleged deception and hint at the complexities of online journalism and the importance of independent income. The piece also emphasizes the challenges and joys of maintaining a free, reader-supported platform.

recent_posts.title: The panic over kids and smartphones has gone too far
recent_posts.summary: Influential figures in politics and media are pushing the narrative that smartphones and social media are causing a mental health crisis among children, leading to moral panic. This is evidenced by Jonathan Haidt's book 'The Anxious Generation,' which has received significant critique. In response, a new YouTube series titled 'tech panic' aims to debunk these myths and provide context on how to truly protect kids online while promoting healthy media use.

recent_posts.title: #129: Nếu bạn buồn vì bị nhận xét là chưa làm tốt ở công ty
recent_posts.summary: Feeling down about negative feedback at work? Remember, your job performance doesn't define your self-worth. Exercise self-compassion by treating yourself as you would a loved one, acknowledge areas for improvement without letting it impact your self-image, and find fulfillment outside of work. Cultivating hobbies and interests can help dissociate negative feedback at work from your overall identity.

recent_posts.title: How to say "No" and win back your time as a software engineer
recent_posts.summary: Sidwyn Koh, a Staff Engineer at Meta, shares strategies on how software engineers can politely say 'no' to save time and focus on their most impactful work. He outlines four approaches: Direct, Redirect, Change Their Perspective, and Stonewall. Additional tips include communicating boundaries, involving managers when overwhelmed, setting focus blocks, documenting knowledge, and balancing when to say 'no' and 'yes.' These tactics help manage responsibilities and maintain a healthy work-life balance.
